method: Inspected ggml-backend.h public API (ggml_backend_tensor_set_async, ggml_backend_tensor_get_async, ggml_backend_synchronize) and the Vulkan backend implementation (ggml-vulkan.cpp): ggml_backend_vk_interface registers real set_tensor_async/get_tensor_async/cpy_tensor_async function pointers (not NULL fallbacks to the sync path) that submit to a Vulkan compute/transfer queue and return without waiting; ggml_backend_vk_synchronize is a real vkQueueWaitIdle-class call, gated by device->support_async (false only on old Intel HW per an in-source comment -- irrelevant to the tested NVIDIA GTX 1650). Empirically confirmed via copybench (sync vs async issue latency) and the prefetch mode (Section 12: measured residual sync_wait_ms after overlapping async copy with a real llama_decode call).

source_evidence.vulkan_backend_todo_comment_text: // TODO: enable async and synchronize (directly above the ggml_backend_vk_interface struct definition)
source_evidence.vulkan_backend_todo_comment_interpretati: Disclosed as-is: llama.cpp upstream itself flags this area with a TODO, even though the async function pointers ARE wired up and DO produce real overlap in our measurements below. Treat the mechanism as functional-but-flagged-unfinished upstream, not as a fully hardened public contract.

classification_basis: ggml_backend_tensor_set_async/get_tensor_async are public ggml-backend.h symbols, the Vulkan backend implements real (non-NULL, non-fallback) async paths, and the prefetch prototype (prefetch_result.json) measured near-zero residual sync_wait_ms when the async copy is issued immediately before a real llama_decode call -- i.e. genuine overlap with GPU decode compute was observed, not just a fast-returning call that still serializes internally.
